corrections_and_extensions: A single finite squared Brownian increment is random: its coefficient of variation does not vanish with dt; the aggregate quadratic-variation sum converges in L2.
The Ito integral of WdW has expectation zero, not zero pathwise value.
The GBM SDE and its exact lognormal transition are the same model; a finite Euler Gaussian step is a numerical approximation, not a second exact model.
Lognormality is conditional on constant-coefficient GBM assumptions, not an empirical universal truth.
Markov modeling does not follow solely from a weak-form market-efficiency slogan.
Endpoint negative cash balance probability is distinct from first-passage insolvency during the year.
Forward-density derivation uses smooth compact-support tests and boundary/integrability assumptions.
